narration: Sunday the twenty-third of November, 2026. In a quiet boardroom, a chair that sat empty for eleven days is pushed back to the table.
picture: The empty CEO chair, black jacket on its back, rolls up to the head of the table.

narration: Nvidia's board has just voted, unanimously, to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately.
picture: Directors raise their hands one by one. A gavel lands.

narration: Six days earlier, the same board had said it did not intend to bring him back at all.
picture: A flashback card: 17 Nov, a speech bubble crossed out.

narration: Shares of the world's most valuable chip company jumped on the news, by more than thirty percent according to CNN.
picture: Bigsby's screen: a green line rockets upward.
flag: REPORTED (one outlet; check the final figure)

narration: The investigation that started it all had not finished. The board said it would carry on to its conclusion.
picture: A thick folder marked INVESTIGATION, still open, sits beside the chair.

narration: So how does a company lose its founder, refuse to take him back, and reverse itself in eleven days?
picture: Title card over the empty chair.

narration: To understand the shock, start with what Huang meant to Nvidia: he co-founded it in 1993 and ran it ever since.
picture: Chip the GPU mascot unrolls a long scroll of years.

narration: Nvidia had become far more than a graphics company. Its chips power much of the world's artificial intelligence.
picture: Chip stands proudly in front of a wall of servers.

narration: Investors treated the founder and the company as almost the same thing. His black leather jacket became a symbol.
picture: The jacket on its hanger glows under a spotlight.

narration: A company that leans that hard on one person is exposed when that person is suddenly in trouble.
picture: The chair wobbles on one leg.

narration: On the eighth of November, according to CNN, the board opened an independent investigation involving its chief executive.
picture: Directors close the boardroom door. A sign flips to PRIVATE.

narration: Word got out. Nvidia shares fell about five percent as the inquiry became public, according to market reports.
picture: Bigsby's screen: a red line dips.

narration: Nobody outside the room yet knew what the investigation was about.
picture: Rita the reporter presses her ear to the boardroom door.

narration: Then the New York Times published its story, and the details landed all at once.
picture: Newspaper slaps onto Rita's desk (generic masthead).

narration: The reports described extramarital affairs. Outlets differed on how many: Variety said several, the Washington Post cited two.
picture: Two newspapers side by side, headlines blurred.

narration: One allegation was far more serious than a personal scandal. It touched national security.
picture: A red DOSSIER envelope slides across the desk.

narration: The Times reported that one woman, a Chinese tech executive, had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.
picture: A shadowy silhouette card, no face, labelled ALLEGED.
flag: ALLEGED (reported by the New York Times)

narration: The reported aim was to learn more about Nvidia's AI chips, the most valuable technology the company has.
picture: Chip the mascot hugs itself nervously.

narration: These were allegations in press reports. The board said it had no reason to believe national security was compromised.
picture: A board statement card, plain type.
on_screen_text: "no reason to believe national security was compromised"

narration: Even the president was unsure. Donald Trump said it was unclear whether the woman was a spy at all.
picture: A generic podium with a microphone (no person) and a question mark.

narration: Uncertainty is poison to a board. Directors had to decide quickly what Nvidia's leader could still do.
picture: Directors around the table, the clock ticking loudly.

narration: On the eleventh, the board accepted Huang's resignation as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately.
picture: The jacket is lifted off the chair. The chair is pushed back.

narration: Nvidia announced it publicly on the twelfth, thanking him for what it called immeasurable contributions to the company.
picture: A press-release card slides in.

narration: Somebody still had to run the company the next morning.
picture: The empty chair, a spotlight on it, an alarm clock ringing.

narration: The board named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim chief executive while it searched for a permanent replacement.
picture: A nameplate card: INTERIM CEO. No portrait.

narration: It also created a new role. Harvey Jones became the first-ever chair of Nvidia's board.
picture: A nameplate card: CHAIR OF THE BOARD. No portrait.

narration: Markets do not wait for searches. Nvidia's stock fell about four percent that Thursday, the Washington Post reported.
picture: Bigsby watches a red candle drop.

narration: CNN put the loss in market value as high as one point seven six trillion dollars, likely over a longer stretch.
picture: A huge stack of coins topples.

narration: Washington was not finished either. Congress summoned Huang to testify, according to CNN.
picture: A domed building with a summons envelope flying from it.

narration: Inside the company, staff wondered whether the founder could ever return.
picture: Dev the engineer stares at the empty chair through a glass door.

narration: On the seventeenth, the answer seemed final. The board said it did not intend to reinstate him.
picture: A board statement card stamped FINAL.

narration: The chairman repeated it on an earnings call, the Yahoo News timeline reported.
picture: A speakerphone on the table; a speech bubble.

narration: One Nvidia employee did not accept that. They built a website with an open letter.
picture: Dev types fast; a web page appears: STAND WITH JENSEN.

narration: The letter asked the board to bring him back while an independent investigation ran its course.
picture: The letter scrolls on Dev's screen.

narration: Signatures poured in: more than one hundred seventy-eight thousand in four days, according to Wikipedia's summary.
picture: A counter spins upward.

narration: Counts kept changing. Fortune later put it above two hundred six thousand names.
picture: The counter ticks past 206,000.

narration: Tom's Guide reported over seventy-five hundred self-identified Nvidia employees among them, and Elon Musk too.
picture: A wall of tiny name tags; one shaped like a rocket.

narration: Online petitions cannot verify who signs them, so these numbers are a mood, not a vote.
picture: A ballot box with a question mark.

narration: Money spoke too. Two well-known tech investors wrote to the board, Reuters reported.
picture: Bigsby writes a letter with a fountain pen.

narration: Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker urged a deliberate process instead of a rushed replacement, keeping a return possible.
picture: The letter folds into a paper plane and flies to the boardroom.

narration: The loudest push came from Washington, on a weekend.
picture: The red phone in the boardroom starts ringing.

narration: On Sunday, Trump posted on Truth Social calling for Huang to be rehired.
picture: A phone screen card with a generic post bubble.

narration: On Monday he told CNBC he had been talking with the board and with Huang, and called the board reasonable.
picture: A TV screen card with a quote bubble (no person drawn).

narration: The Verge reported he personally lobbied directors over that weekend.
picture: The red phone rings at each director's seat in turn.
flag: REPORTED (via a summary of The Verge)

narration: A president pressing a private company's board is highly unusual, and critics said so.
picture: Rita reads a stack of opinion pages, eyebrows raised.

narration: On the twenty-third, the board met again, and this time the vote went the other way, unanimously.
picture: The hands go up again. The jacket goes back on the chair.

narration: Its filing said the board was satisfied with Huang's candor and ability to lead Nvidia.
picture: Quote card from the filing.

narration: The same filing added a striking line: the board had received input from senior levels of the United States government.
picture: The red phone sits on the table, receiver off the hook.
on_screen_text: "input from senior levels of the United States government"

narration: Investors cheered. CNN reported the shares soared more than thirty percent, one of the stock's best days on record.
picture: Bigsby throws ticker tape in the air.

narration: The cheer did not last. In later sessions the stock fell again, by between four and seven percent.
picture: The ticker tape stops; Bigsby looks at a dipping line.

narration: One estimate put that pullback at three to four hundred and fifty billion dollars in market value.
picture: A melting stack of coins.

narration: Returning to the job is not the same as being cleared. CBC stressed that Huang had not been exonerated.
picture: The chair has a sticky note: NOT CLEARED.

narration: The board's own investigation, opened on the eighth, had no announced end date.
picture: The INVESTIGATION folder grows thicker; a calendar with no end.

narration: Reports listed the SEC, the FBI and California's attorney general among those involved in inquiries.
picture: Three generic official seals (no real logos) on a card.

narration: Asked on Fox News whether Huang had been cleared, Attorney General Todd Blanche would not even acknowledge an investigation.
picture: A podium card with a closed door.

narration: Critics in Congress were furious. Hakeem Jeffries called the reinstatement indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.
picture: A quote card in red.

narration: Supporters saw it differently: a founder back at work, and a company steadied.
picture: Dev and staff cheer quietly at their desks.

narration: The episode left an uneasy question about who really decides who runs a company: its board, its staff, or the government.
picture: Three arrows point at the chair: BOARD, STAFF, WASHINGTON.

narration: Some analysts warned the precedent may outlast this one chief executive.
picture: A long shadow stretches from the chair across the floor.

narration: Governance experts also note that a single irreplaceable leader is itself a risk the board must plan for.
picture: Chip draws a succession chart with only one box.

narration: So, what is confirmed? Nvidia's filings confirm the resignation, the interim leadership, and the unanimous reinstatement.
picture: A checklist with three green ticks.

narration: The spying claim remains an allegation from press reports, and investigations are still running.
picture: A checklist line with a yellow question mark.

narration: We found no public statement from Huang addressing the allegations in the sources we checked for this video.
picture: A blank speech bubble over the empty chair.

narration: Eleven days were enough to show how fast a single story can move a trillion-dollar company.
picture: A calendar flips through eleven pages in a blur.

narration: Back in the boardroom, the folder stays open on the table, right next to the chair.
picture: Final shot: the jacket on the chair, the open folder beside it, lights dimming.
